ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit Against Anthropic
ip_top_stories.summary: Major publishers and media groups have filed support for Concord Music Group's lawsuit against Anthropic, broadening industry opposition to the AI company's alleged copyright infringement. The move signals a coordinated effort by rights holders across publishing and music to challenge AI training practices. The story is reported by Publishers Weekly.

ip_top_stories.title: Penguin to Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Version of German Children's Book
ip_top_stories.summary: German children's book publisher Penguin is pursuing legal action against OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT reproduced content from a copyrighted children's book without authorisation. The case adds to a growing wave of European publisher litigation against AI companies over training data and output reproduction. Multiple sources confirm the filing.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's Amodei Seeks Copyright Deal That 'Works for Everyone'
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called for a copyright framework that balances the interests of AI developers and rights holders, commenting specifically in the context of an Australian copyright dispute. His remarks suggest Anthropic is open to negotiated licensing arrangements rather than purely litigating fair use defences. The story is reported by multiple outlets.

ip_top_stories.title: UK Government Maintains Status Quo on AI and Copyright, Playing the Long Game on Potential Reform
ip_top_stories.summary: The UK government has opted to maintain existing copyright rules rather than introduce immediate reform to address AI training data, signalling a cautious approach while longer-term policy options remain under consideration. The decision follows significant pressure from creators and rights holders who had pushed for stronger protections. The story is covered by legal and publishing press.

ip_top_stories.title: French Private Members' Bill Aims to Protect Creatives' Copyright from AI Usage
ip_top_stories.summary: A private members' bill has been introduced in the French legislature seeking to protect the copyright of creative professionals against unauthorised use of their works for AI training. The bill reflects growing legislative momentum in Europe to give rights holders greater control over how their content is used by AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: What AI Asks of Open Access
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI's appetite for training data is creating new tensions and questions for the open access publishing model.

ip_further_links.title: Q&A: The UK's Copyright Report — A Gift to Creators, A Problem for AI
ip_further_links.summary: A legal Q&A analyses the UK's recent copyright report, arguing it favours creators but poses significant challenges for AI developers seeking to use copyrighted material for training.

ip_further_links.title: Cloudflare Legal Chief on AI Bots and Publisher Revenue Loss
ip_further_links.summary: Cloudflare's chief legal officer discusses how AI crawlers are affecting publisher revenues and the company's approach to managing bot access and overblocking.

ip_further_links.title: Is Copyright Law the Wrong Weapon Against AI?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis questions whether copyright litigation is the most effective legal tool to regulate AI training practices, suggesting alternative regulatory frameworks may be needed.

ip_further_links.title: How African Creators Are Currently Being Exploited in the AI Boom
ip_further_links.summary: An investigation into how African creators' works are being used without consent or compensation to train AI models, with little legal recourse available.

ip_further_links.title: Beyond Copyright: Why Asia Pacific Governments Must Govern AI Training Data as Public Infrastructure
ip_further_links.summary: A policy commentary argues that Asia Pacific governments should treat AI training data governance as a public infrastructure issue, going beyond copyright frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Harlequin to Co-Produce AI-Generated 'Microdramas'
ip_further_links.summary: Publisher Harlequin has announced plans to co-produce a slate of AI-generated short-form dramatic content, marking a notable move by a major trade publisher into AI-created media.

ip_further_links.title: AI Law in Canada Is Evolving Through Familiar Principles
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis examines how Canadian courts and regulators are applying existing intellectual property and privacy principles to emerging AI copyright disputes.

ip_further_links.title: How India Is Trying to Navigate AI Copyright's Three-Body Problem
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of India's approach to balancing the competing interests of AI developers, rights holders, and the public in formulating AI copyright policy.

ip_further_links.title: Generative AI and Copyright: Emerging Legal and Policy Questions for Africa's Creative Industries
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of the legal and policy challenges that generative AI poses for copyright protection in African creative industries.
